source_documents.title: PET-Driven Fluorescence Modulation in Halochromic Styryl Hemicyanine Dyes Targeting DNA Minor Groove

reference_evidence_units.quote: The fluorescence quenching is attributed to the PET effect from the nitrogen atoms of the piperazine substituent, as demonstrated by theoretical computations.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyes 4a-4c
reference_evidence_units.conditions: TE buffer (pH 8), with and without dsDNA
reference_evidence_units.statement: Weak intrinsic fluorescence is attributed to PET from the piperazine nitrogens.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Mechanistic assignment by the authors, supported by orbital energies, not by a direct ET measurement.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The titration with hydrochloric acid enhances fluorescence of dyes in solution and their respective dye–DNA complexes, providing further evidence for the intramolecular PET effect.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyes 4a-4c
reference_evidence_units.conditions: TE buffer titrated with HCl; dye-DNA complexes titrated with HCl
reference_evidence_units.statement: Protonation (HCl) restores fluorescence of the free dyes and of their DNA complexes.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Protonation also changes conjugation and geometry, so the recovery is not specific to PET alone.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The lone pair orbitals of the amino groups in the receptor are of higher energies than those of the fluorophore, which is a precondition for a typical reductive photoinduced electron transfer process.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dye 4c
reference_evidence_units.statement: The receptor (piperazine) HOMO lies between the fluorophore HOMO-1 and LUMO, allowing reductive PET.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Hence, the HOMO-1 → LUMO transition is classified as an internal charge transfer (ICT) transition.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dye 4c
reference_evidence_units.statement: The main absorption band is an ICT transition from the N-phenylpiperazine donor to the benzothiazolium acceptor.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Concerns absorption; the paper does not attribute the emission behaviour to ICT.

reference_evidence_units.quote: All dyes exhibit negative solvatochromism when going from nonpolar to polar solvents (e.g., from toluene to DMSO).
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyes 4a-4c
reference_evidence_units.conditions: H2O, DMF, DMSO, EtOH, CH2Cl2, CHCl3, toluene
reference_evidence_units.statement: Strong negative absorption solvatochromism, consistent with a charge-transfer transition.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The dyes exhibit a single absorption band in the visible region, ruling out the possibility of aggregate formation under the experimental conditions.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyes 4a-4c
reference_evidence_units.statement: No aggregation in buffer at the working concentrations.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Toluene is an outlier that the authors tentatively attribute to stacking or H-aggregates; emission there is not analysed.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The absorption band is assigned as ICT with negative solvatochromism; not used to explain the emission switching.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Fluorescence quenching attributed to reductive PET from the piperazine donor; acid restores emission; orbital energetics support PET.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT

mechanism_decisions.label: ESIPT_PT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No intramolecular proton donor-acceptor pair (no OH/NH adjacent to an acceptor).

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Fluorescence quenching attributed to reductive PET from the piperazine donor; acid restores emission; orbital energetics support PET.
